1|# Anamnesis contract (v3.7, 28 Oct 2026)
2|
3|A pre-visit intake agent. It takes the patient's voice note (Voice Transcribe supports 25 languages; **tested live so far only on synthetic text-to-speech notes: English, and Egyptian Arabic text with brand names in Latin or Arabic script, spoken by a macOS voice; no human speech yet**) and photos of their medicine packs (tested live on rendered test packs and, from batch 21, public photos of real packs: Wikimedia Commons, DailyMed and Cairo University), and gives the clinician a one-page brief. Every fact in the brief links to the audio turn and the image region it came from. **It reports where sources disagree. It never gives medical advice.** The voice notes are synthetic so far; the photos of real packs are public, and Ahmed's own photos and voice, when recorded, follow `docs/DATA_HANDLING.md` (batch 23, QM M5 #2).
4|
5|## 1. Evidence (independent IDs, no forced chain)
6|| Model | Fields | Rules |
7||---|---|---|
8|| `AudioTurn` | `turn_id`, `start_ms`, `end_ms`, `transcript`, `speaker?`, `lang_hint?` | `end_ms > start_ms ≥ 0`. Turn-level timing only (Voice Transcribe has no word timestamps) |
9|| `ImageRegion` | `region_id`, `image_sha256`, `object_id`, `x1,y1,x2,y2`, `frame_w`, `frame_h`, `confidence?` | Source pixels, inclusive corners (SAM 3.1 format). `0 ≤ x1 ≤ x2 < frame_w`, same for y. `confidence` in [0,1]. Hash is 64 lowercase hex chars |
10|
11|## 2. Medication facts
12|| Model | Fields | Rules |
13||---|---|---|
14|| `IngredientAmount` | `inn`, `salt?`, `amount`, `unit` | `amount > 0` (Decimal). `unit` ∈ `mg, mcg, g, ml, iu`. `inn` holds the **active moiety**: a curated alias table splits salt names (`"Metoprolol succinate"` → `inn="metoprolol"`, `salt="succinate"`). Synonyms are handled the same way (acetaminophen → paracetamol). So are the French, Spanish, German and Latin forms that packs print for the catalogue's ingredients (batch 21, staged cases U2 and U8): `amoxicilline`, `amoxicilina`, `amoxicillinum`; `acide clavulanique`, `ácido clavulánico`, `Clavulansäure`, `acidum clavulanicum`; `paracétamol`, `paracetamolum`; `métoprolol`, `metoprololum`, `metoprololi succinas`, `Metoprololsuccinat`, `metoprololi tartras`, `Metoprololtartrat`; `bisoprololum`, `bisoprololi fumaras`, `Bisoprololfumarat`; `amlodipino`, `amlodipinum`, `amlodipini besilas`, `Amlodipinbesilat`; `metformina`, `metformine`, `metforminum`, `metformini hydrochloridum`, `Metforminhydrochlorid`; `atorvastatina`, `atorvastatine`, `atorvastatinum`, `atorvastatinum calcicum`; `caféine`, `cafeína`, `Coffein`, `coffeinum`. Each salt form gives the same moiety and salt as its English one. Keys match after Unicode NFC normalisation, so decomposed accents resolve too (supervisor 21 #7). An unknown suffix is never stripped |
15|| `Strength` | `ingredients: list[IngredientAmount]`, `per`, `release` | ≥1 ingredient (combinations: Augmentin 875/125) and **no duplicate canonical INNs**. `per` ∈ `tablet, capsule, ml, dose`. `release` ∈ `immediate, modified, unknown` (default `unknown`) |
16|| `DoseRegimen` | `units_per_intake?`, `intakes_per_day?`, `as_needed?` | Decimals > 0 when present (0.5 means half a tablet). `as_needed` defaults to `None`: unknown, not "no" |
17|| `PatientClaim` (from audio) | `claim_id`, `name_text`, `inn?`, `strength?`, `intake_amount?`, `regimen?`, `status`, `audio_evidence` | `audio_evidence` has ≥1 turn_id. `status` ∈ `active, discontinued, unknown`. `intake_amount` (what they take per intake) is kept separate from `strength` (what the tablet contains) |
18|| `PackObservation` (from image) | `observation_id`, `label_text?`, `inn?`, `strength?`, `readability`, `country?`, `visual_evidence` | `visual_evidence` has ≥1 region_id. `readability` ∈ `readable, partial, unreadable`. `readable` requires `label_text` |
19|
20|`AudioTurn.transcript` and `speaker` are non-empty when present.
21|
22|### Model replies (batch 16)
23|Every string a model writes is checked at the parser, before it can reach a report:
24|- **Numbers** arrive as strings. `"2.5"` and the decimal comma `"2,5"` both parse; a comma is a decimal mark only when 1–2 digits follow it (`"1,000"` is ambiguous and does not parse). A dot followed by exactly three digits with a non-zero whole part (`"1.000"`, `"2.500"`) is ambiguous the same way (a European thousands mark) and does not parse; `"0.125"` does. Ranges (`"1-2"`), words, zero and negatives don't parse. The Arabic decimal sign `٫` (U+066B) is read as a dot, under the same rules, and Arabic-Indic digits parse like ASCII ones (`"٢٫٥"` is 2.5, `"١٠٠"` is 100); the Arabic thousands sign `٬` doesn't parse (QM M4 code #3; batch 19.1). **Digits are exactly three sets:** ASCII `0–9`, Arabic-Indic `٠–٩` (U+0660–U+0669) and extended Arabic-Indic `۰–۹` (U+06F0–U+06F9), so `"۵"` is 5 and `"۲٫۵"` is 2.5. `catalogue.normalise` maps both Arabic-Indic sets to ASCII as well (batch 23, QM M5 #6). Any other digit (`"５"`, `"५"`) doesn't parse (QM M4 code round 2 #2; batch 21). **A single number word, the whole amount, parses as its value** (batch 22, live 28 Oct: Spark still sometimes writes "five"). So "five" is 5, «خمسة» 5, «خمسمية» 500 and «واحد» 1. Two or more words never parse ("five hundred", "eight seventy-five", «خمسة وعشرين»), and neither do zero, half, hundred and thousand words on their own. The word must be bare, letters only (tatweel allowed): with a sign, a comparator, punctuation or any tashkeel it never parses, so "<five" ("less than five") is not 5 and «خُمس» (a fifth) is not «خمس» (five) (batch 22 round 2, supervisor finding 1). The stated-amount check still applies.
25|- **An optional field that doesn't parse becomes null; it never fails the whole reply.** Optional fields: `regimen.units_per_intake`, `regimen.intakes_per_day`, `intake_amount` (null if its amount doesn't parse or it fails validation, e.g. an empty `inn`), `strength` (null if any of its ingredient amounts doesn't parse, or if it fails validation, e.g. an equivalence line read as two salts of one INN), and the label's `country`.
26|- **A dropped claim amount takes the other one with it.** When a claim's reply sent a `strength` or an `intake_amount` and either one is dropped, both become null, so the claim can't reach `match` on what is left (supervisor 16 #1: a combination whose caffeine amount didn't parse, or an intake range, would otherwise have matched). From batch 17, rule 8 also uses `regimen.units_per_intake`, so a sent `units_per_intake` that is dropped (`"1-2"`, `"half or one"`) nulls `strength` and `intake_amount` the same way.
27|- **Ingredient fields are grounded (batch 24).** Live on 29 Oct, Spark labelled a 5 mg intake "string", the schema's type name, and the checks kept it (`evidence/finetune/results.md`).
28|  - **The fields:** the claim's `inn`, `intake_amount.inn`, and each strength ingredient's `inn`.
29|  - **A field is grounded** when, after `catalogue.normalise`, either:
30|    - it is a run of whole words in a turn the claim cites (an Arabic word may carry one of the attached clitics `catalogue.ARABIC_CLITICS`, the release words' rule);
31|    - or each of its words, with one final vowel removed when it has 6 letters or more, begins a word of such a turn. A word under 3 letters must be a whole word of the turn, so "vitamin d" isn't grounded by "de" (round 4, #4). The field and the turns are read in NFC (round 5, #4). So "metformin" is grounded by "metformina" and "amlodipine" by "amlodipino", as patients name ingredients in Spanish.
32|    - **or its `canonical_inn` and `salt_of` pair equals that of a word or a run of up to three words in such a turn** (round 2, supervisor #3). So a salt said inside a German compound grounds it: "Metoprololtartrat" grounds "metoprolol tartrate".
33|    - **or, for an amount label only,** its `canonical_inn` is an ingredient of the catalogue entry the claim's `name_text` resolves to. A combination is said by its brand ("Augmentin, eight hundred seventy-five and one hundred twenty-five milligrams"), so its labels name the catalogue's ingredients, and a curated salt such as "Bisoprolol fumarate" for Concor is kept. The claim's own `inn` is grounded by the turns only. (CEO's reference build, 29 Oct: without this, the combination and salt pins of batches 8 and 21 fail.)
34|  - **A field made only of digits, unit words or number words** ("50", "mg", "5 mg", "cinco") is never grounded. For this check, the English unit words (`milligram(s)`, `gram(s)`, `microgram(s)`, `millilitre(s)`, `milliliter(s)`, `unit(s)`, `iu`) and the joiners `and`, `y`, `und`, `a`, `point`, `coma` and `komma` count as amount words too (round 2, #7). So does any word the number reader gives a role, even one that needs a neighbour (`mil`, `ein`, `cero`, `zero`), and German `null` (round 3, #2).
35|  - **An ungrounded claim `inn` becomes null.**
36|  - **An empty or ungrounded amount label** is relabelled before validation, to the claim's grounded `inn` or, if there is none, its `name_text`. `parse_claims_json` takes an optional `catalogue`; without one it uses the bundled catalogue.
37|  - **Relabelling never drops an amount.** The resolver then reads a longer label as it reads any name: "Concor 5 mg" resolves to bisoprolol.
38|  - **Two lines for one ingredient (round 2, supervisor #1).**
39|    - **The rule:** after relabelling, a strength whose lines resolve, as the reconciler resolves them, to fewer ingredients than it has lines is dropped, and the drop takes the intake with it.
40|    - **The second layer:** the reconciler's `_identity` also reports a conflict for such a strength, which gives `insufficient_information`.
41|    - **The case it closes:** an unsaid "caffeine" relabelled "Panadol" next to "paracetamol" 500 mg reached `match` against a Panadol 500 mg pack.
42|- **An empty strength is no strength (batch 24).** A `strength` whose `ingredients` is an empty list becomes null without counting as a dropped amount, so the `intake_amount` stays.
43|  - **Its `release` isn't kept.** The claim's release then comes from the release words or the brand, as for any claim without a strength.

344|## 4. Agent loop (`anamnesis/agent/`, batches 14 and 15.5)
345|`run_intake(audio, images, ...)` runs a **fixed order**; no model chooses actions, nothing a model wrote is surfaced except source data (transcripts, label text), and there are no outer retries (adapters retry once themselves).
346|0. **Prepare** every photo before any model sees it (`prepare_image(data, mime) -> (data, mime)`, `anamnesis/agent/media.py`). Phones store the pixels sideways and record the turn in EXIF; SAM applies it and Spark does not (live, 27 Oct: on a portrait photo, 2 of 3 labels were read from the wrong pack). Preparation turns the pixels upright for every EXIF orientation (1–8) and drops all metadata (EXIF including GPS and camera tags, XMP, IPTC, ICC profiles, comments, PNG text chunks, and any extra frames such as an HDR gain map), so SAM, Spark, the crop and the brief see the same pixels and no location leaves the machine. A JPEG or PNG that is already upright and carries none of these is returned byte for byte. Otherwise a JPEG (including a multi-picture MPO, primary frame only) is re-encoded as JPEG (quality 95, 4:4:4 chroma), and anything else as PNG. Preparation is deterministic and idempotent; region hashes and `intake_id` use the prepared bytes, and callers that show a photo (the brief) show the prepared bytes. Bytes that can't be decoded raise `ValueError`; the loop then logs one `segment` step `error: image cannot be decoded` with no call ids, sends that photo to no model, and goes on with the next.
347|1. `transcribe` if there is audio. 2. `extract_claims` if there are turns.
348|3. Per image, `segment` with each concept in order (`medicine box`, `label`, `package`), stopping at the first that returns a region. `package` came in batch 23: on 28 Oct SAM 3.1 found no region with the first two in 19 of 30 Cairo University phone photos, `package` found one in all 19, and Spark 1.3 read 15 of those crops right (`evidence/batches/22/comparison.md`).
349|4. **Read the crop first (Z8, batch 18).** For each of the `top_regions(k=3)` of each image: only regions whose `image_sha256` and frame size match the prepared photo are kept, ranked and published in the report; each other region gets one `read` step `error: region does not match the photo` and is dropped. Each kept region is cut with `crop_region` (padded by 5% of the box size on each side, i.e. 10% in total, rounded down and clamped to the frame; refused unless the sha256 and frame size match the region) and the reader is called on the **crop only**, as PNG, with `cropped=True`. The reader never sees the full photo, so a reading can only describe the pixels of its own region (provenance by construction; live, 27 Oct: 8/8 crop reads correct at 465–1,001 input tokens against about 4,300 for the full photo). A crop that fails logs one `read` step `error: crop failed` (no provider call) and the region gets no reading. Once the session is exhausted, no crop is cut and nothing is logged.
350|5. Each `unreadable` or `partial` reading gets **one** `zoom_read`: the same crop, upscaled 2× (Lanczos; the factor is lowered so the longest side is at most 2,048 px; if that factor is ≤ 1 there is no zoom and no step), read with `cropped=True`. The new reading keeps the **source** `region_id`, so provenance stays in source pixels. SAM never runs on a crop. At most 2 reads per region (`max_grounding_iters = 2`). Both the read and the zoom cut their crop through the name `crop_region` in `anamnesis/agent/loop.py`.
351|6. `reconcile` with `reconcile_all`.
352|- **Budget:** every provider call, including failed ones, counts 1 against `max_provider_calls`. Its default (batch 23 round 2, supervisor 23 #3) is enough for every call the loop can make: 2 for the voice note, plus, per photo, one per concept and two per region (a read and a zoom), so `2 + (len(concepts) + 2 × top_k) × photos`, 29 for three photos with the defaults. The dollar caps (`SessionGuard`) bound the spend. With a fixed 12, batch 23's third concept ran the budget out on a four-photo intake, and a pack the patient had sent was reported as not photographed. An explicit `max_provider_calls` still sets the budget. Without a dollar cap the default grows with the number of photos, so every caller that spends real money wraps the providers in a `SessionGuard` with `max_usd` (`scripts/intake_live.py` does, with `--session-usd`; supervisor 23 round 2 #4). The call that would exceed it is skipped, a `budget_exhausted` step is logged (it is then the last step, whatever fails afterwards, including a crop), and every remaining provider call is skipped. Reconciliation still runs on what exists.
353|- **Errors:** a provider error becomes a step whose `outcome` is `error: <provider> <ExceptionName>` (no message text); the loop continues with the next item.
354|- **Report** (batch 20 adds `superseded`, §8): one `ReconciliationReport` (`anamnesis/schema/report.py`): turns, claims, regions, observations (`o0, o1, ...` in reading order, `visual_evidence=[region_id]`), findings, steps, `calls`, `spend_usd` (sum of `cost_usd + prior_cost_usd` over every returned trace) and a sha256 `intake_id` of the inputs. A validator rejects any evidence, claim or observation id that points nowhere.
355|- **Each step records its call** (batch 23): `model_id` (`None` without a trace), `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `latency_ms` (0 without a trace), and `cost_usd`, everything the step was charged: `cost_usd + prior_cost_usd` of its trace, or the `charged_usd` of a failed call. The model, tokens and latency come from the returned trace, or from a failed call's `attempt_trace` when it has one. So the steps add up to `spend_usd`, also after `add_photo` (§8). A step without a call costs 0, and a step from before batch 23 loads with these defaults. A step's `model_id` with `-contributor` anywhere, in any case, is refused.
356|- **Session caps:** `SessionGuard(parent, max_usd, max_calls)` wraps the ledger guard with a per-session dollar and call cap and still writes every charge to the parent.

460|**Cross-medication observations** (`cross_medication(claims, catalogue)` in `anamnesis/core/overlap.py`; supervisor #2, J2). Pairwise reconciliation can't see two medicines that overlap each other: the showcase patient reports Concor and Beloc-Zok, two beta-blockers. Only **claims** count, never the photos, because a pack can't show use and repeated photos never imply duplicate use.
461|- A claim counts unless its status is `discontinued`, and only if its identity set (§3) can be built. **A claim with an extraction conflict counts only by the ingredients its identity set shares with the catalogue entry its `name_text` resolves to.** When the name doesn't resolve to one entry, or they share none, it doesn't count. An observation built on one of two disagreeing readings could name the wrong medicine (QM M4 code #2; supervisor 19.1 #2):
462|  - "Concor" with a metoprolol strength doesn't count, rather than being listed as metoprolol;
463|  - "Panadol" with a paracetamol + caffeine strength counts as paracetamol. Its *product* is the catalogue brand when `name_text` matches a brand or alias name, otherwise `normalise(name_text)`. A brand said twice, in either script, is one product.
464|- `same_ingredient`: for each INN, the counted claims whose identity set contains it, when they name 2+ different products (Panadol + Gelocatil, Panadol + "paracetamol", Panadol + Panadol Extra).
465|- `same_class`: for each class in the curated `DRUG_CLASSES` (only `beta-blockers`: bisoprolol, metoprolol), the counted claims whose identity set contains a member, when they hold 2+ different members and name 2+ different products.
466|- One observation per INN or class, with `kind`, `key` (the INN or the class name), `claim_ids` (sorted), the claims' `audio_evidence` (sorted, no repeats) and its `note`. Order: `same_ingredient` by key, then `same_class` by key.
467|- Notes (fixed): `same_ingredient`: "More than one product the patient mentioned, and did not report as stopped, contains this ingredient. Concurrent use is unconfirmed." `same_class`: "More than one medicine the patient mentioned, and did not report as stopped, belongs to this class. Concurrent use is unconfirmed."
468|- In the brief, each observation is `<article data-kind="<kind>">` in `across`, with its note, its key, and each claim's `name_text` linked to that claim's turns.
469|
470|**Coverage** (`coverage_lines(report, images, audio) -> list[str]`; supervisor #4, Z5: a photo where nothing was found is never silent). A photo is prepared as the loop does it: `prepare_image`, then decoded; a `ValueError` or `OSError` means it could not be opened. A photo's `segment` steps are those whose target starts with the first 12 hex characters of its prepared sha256 followed by ":". Each line is one `<li>` of the `coverage` section. The lines, in order:
471|1. `Photos received: <n>.`
472|2. One line per photo, in input order from 1, the first that applies:
473|   - `Photo <i>: could not be opened; no model saw it.`
474|   - `Photo <i>: not examined; the call budget ran out first.` (no `segment` step for it)
475|   - `Photo <i>: pack detection failed.` (every `segment` step for it is an error)
476|   - `Photo <i>: no pack found.` (no report region on it)
477|   - `Photo <i>: packs found <r>, labels read <o>, not fully readable <u>.` (r report regions on it, o observations of those regions, u of them `unreadable` or `partial`)
478|3. The voice note, the first that applies: `Voice note: none.` (no audio), `Voice note: not transcribed.` (no turns), `Voice note: turns <t>; medicines could not be extracted.` (the `extract_claims` step is missing or an error), `Voice note: turns <t>, medicines mentioned <c>.`
479|4. Only when the report has a `budget_exhausted` step: `The intake stopped early: the call budget ran out, so later steps were skipped.`
480|
481|**How it got here** (batch 23). After the last section and before the script, one `<details id="timeline">`, collapsed (no `open` attribute), so the page still has exactly the sections above. Its `<summary>` is `TIMELINE_HEADING` ("How it got here"), then one `<table>`:
482|- `<thead>`: one row of `<th>`, the `TIMELINE_COLUMNS`: `#`, `Step`, `Target`, `Outcome`, `Model`, `Tokens in`, `Tokens out`, `Time`, `Cost`.
483|- `<tbody>`: one row of `<td>` per report step, in order: `n`, the action, the target, the outcome; then the model, tokens in, tokens out, and the time in seconds with one decimal (`6.5 s`), each `TIMELINE_NONE` (`—`) when the step has no `model_id`; then the cost, `$` and the amount formatted `.5f` (`$0.00811`).
484|- `<tfoot>`: one row with one cell, `TIMELINE_TOTAL` (`Total: {calls} calls, ${usd}`) with the report's `calls` and its `spend_usd` formatted `.5f`.
485|Every value is HTML-escaped; the labels are fixed templates in `anamnesis/schema/templates.py`. Nothing a model wrote appears here.
486|
487|**Scope lines**, in the header, always (supervisor #3, #4):
488|- "Anamnesis reports where the patient's account and the pack photos disagree. It gives no medical advice."
489|- "Prescribed directions, timing, adherence and supply were not assessed."
490|- "Over-the-counter, herbal and non-tablet products may be missing from this brief: ask about them."
491|- "Checks across medicines cover shared ingredients and one curated class (beta-blockers); interactions were not assessed." (QM M4 code #8; batch 19.1)
492|
493|**Catalogue:** one synthetic entry for the hero case (J2): Gelocatil (ES; paracetamol; immediate release; splittability unknown; Arabic aliases جيلوكاتيل and جلوكاتيل).
494|
495|**Review (batch 20):** the review status, open photo requests, replaced packs and the request count on the brief are specified in §8 "On the brief".
496|
497|**The look (batch 25).** The page's one `<style>` was redesigned in batch 25, and the head gained one tag, `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`, right after `<meta charset="utf-8">`: without it a phone lays the page out 980 px wide and shrinks it, so the narrow-screen rule never applied. Nothing else changed: the same report gives the same page outside the style and that tag, word for word and tag for tag, with the same script (the contract pins hashes of five briefs rendered before the batch, with the style removed). The style loads nothing (no `url(`, `@import` or `@font-face`) and uses system fonts. It adds no words, since a `content` value is only ever empty, and it hides nothing. A photo box keeps its transparent fill, so the whole box stays clickable; `fill:none` would leave only its outline clickable. Text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text), and disagreements keep the amber accent `#d9480f`. The two sides stack below 640 px and stay side by side in print. Nothing makes the page wider than the screen; the timeline table scrolls inside its own box. Light theme only.
498|
499|## 8. Clinician review and photo requests (`anamnesis/review.py`, batch 20)
500|Nothing in a brief is final until a clinician approves it. Before approving, the clinician can ask the patient for **one new photo** of a pack that couldn't be read, or of a medicine the patient mentioned but didn't photograph. Only that photo is processed, and the intake continues from the saved report. This is the workshop's "the run pauses for a person, then resumes", without letting a model choose anything: the clinician chooses, and the code checks the choice is allowed.

220|def _grounded_by_turns(field: object, cited: list[str]) -> bool:
221|    """An ingredient field grounded by cited turns (SPEC §2, batch 24)."""
222|    if not isinstance(field, str):
223|        return False
224|    norm_field = normalise(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", field))
225|    if not norm_field:
226|        return False
227|    field_words = norm_field.split()
228|    only_numbers = True
229|    for word in field_words:
230|        if word in UNIT_WORDS or word in _AMOUNT_ONLY_WORDS or stated_amounts(word) or has_number_role(word):
231|            continue
232|        if word.isdigit():
233|            continue
234|        only_numbers = False
235|        break
236|    if only_numbers:
237|        return False
238|    field_pair = (canonical_inn(field), salt_of(field))
239|    for text in cited:
240|        norm_turn = normalise(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text))
241|        if not norm_turn:
242|            continue
243|        parts = []
244|        for word in field_words:
245|            if re.search(r"[\u0600-\u06ff]", word):
246|                parts.append(f"{ARABIC_CLITICS}{re.escape(word)}")
247|            else:
248|                parts.append(re.escape(word))
249|        if re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + r"\s+".join(parts) + r"(?!\w)", norm_turn):
250|            return True
251|        turn_words = norm_turn.split()
252|        matched = True
253|        for word in field_words:
254|            if len(word) < 3:
255|                if word not in turn_words:
256|                    matched = False
257|                    break
258|                continue
259|            stem = word[:-1] if len(word) >= 6 and word[-1] in "aeiou" else word
260|            if not any(turn_word.startswith(stem) for turn_word in turn_words):
261|                matched = False
262|                break
263|        if matched:
264|            return True
265|        for start in range(len(turn_words)):
266|            for size in (1, 2, 3):
267|                run = " ".join(turn_words[start:start + size])
268|                if not run:
269|                    continue
270|                if (canonical_inn(run), salt_of(run)) == field_pair:
271|                    return True
272|    return False

387|class MetaClaimExtractor:
388|    def __init__(
389|        self, client: MetaClient, guard: SpendGuard, model: str = "muse-spark-1.3",
390|    ) -> None:
391|        if "-contributor" in model.strip().casefold():
392|            raise ValueError("contributor models are not permitted")
393|        self.client = client
394|        self.guard = guard
395|        self.model = model
396|
397|    def extract(self, turns: list[AudioTurn]) -> tuple[list[PatientClaim], ProviderTrace | None]:
398|        if not turns:
399|            return [], None
400|
401|        transcript = "\n".join(
402|            f"[{turn.turn_id} {turn.start_ms}–{turn.end_ms} ms, speaker {turn.speaker or 'unknown'}] "
403|            f"{turn.transcript}"
404|            for turn in turns
405|        )
406|        body = {
407|            "model": self.model,
408|            "reasoning_effort": "low",
409|            "max_tokens": 16000,
410|            "messages": [
411|                {"role": "system", "content": _SYSTEM_PROMPT},
412|                {"role": "user", "content": transcript},
413|            ],
414|            "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {
415|                "name": "patient_claims", "strict": True, "schema": CLAIMS_SCHEMA,
416|            }},
417|        }
418|
419|        estimate = spark_call_estimate(body)
420|
421|        def attempt() -> tuple[list[PatientClaim], ProviderTrace]:
422|            self.guard.check(estimate)
423|            payload, latency_ms = self.client.post("/chat/completions", json=body)
424|            try:
425|                usage = payload["usage"]
426|                input_tokens = int(usage["prompt_tokens"])
427|                output_tokens = int(usage["completion_tokens"])
428|                content = payload["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
429|                call_id = payload["id"]
430|                if not isinstance(call_id, str) or not call_id:
431|                    raise ValueError("missing id")
432|                cost = cost_usd(self.model, input_tokens=input_tokens, output_tokens=output_tokens)
433|            except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
434|                raise ProviderError(
435|                    "spark", "malformed Spark response", retryable=True,
436|                    billable_uncertain=True, estimated_reason="malformed Spark response",
437|                ) from exc
438|            trace = ProviderTrace(
439|                call_id=call_id,
440|                model_id=self.model,
441|                latency_ms=latency_ms,
442|                input_tokens=input_tokens,
443|                output_tokens=output_tokens,
444|                cost_usd=cost,
445|            )
446|            self.guard.charge_prechecked(trace)
447|            if payload["choices"][0].get("finish_reason") == "length":
448|                raise ProviderError(
449|                    "spark", "Spark reply stopped at the length limit", retryable=False,
450|                    attempt_trace=trace,
451|                )
452|            try:
453|                claims = parse_claims_json(content, turns)
454|            except ProviderError as exc:
455|                raise ProviderError(
456|                    exc.provider, self.client._safe(str(exc)), retryable=True,
457|                    attempt_trace=trace,
458|                ) from None
459|            return claims, trace
460|
461|        return with_one_retry(attempt, guard=self.guard, model_id=self.model, estimate=estimate)

21|def claim(name, *, intake_amount=None, strength=None, units=None, per_day=None, status="active", inn=None,
22|          turn_ids=("turn-0",)):
23|    return {"name_text": name, "inn": inn, "strength": strength, "intake_amount": intake_amount,
24|            "regimen": {"units_per_intake": units, "intakes_per_day": per_day, "as_needed": None},
25|            "status": status, "turn_ids": list(turn_ids)}

36|def parse(texts, *claims):
37|    texts = texts if isinstance(texts, tuple) else (texts,)
38|    return parse_claims_json(json.dumps({"claims": list(claims)}, ensure_ascii=False), turns(*texts))

41|def intake_of(texts, *claims, index=0):
42|    """The intake amount the checks keep for one claim, or None."""
43|    kept = parse(texts, *claims)[index].intake_amount
44|    return None if kept is None else kept.amount

174|    if token in ("hundert", "tausend"):

177|    value = 0
178|    for word in sorted(GERMAN_MULTIPLIERS, key=len, reverse=True):
179|        if rest.startswith(word + "tausend"):
180|            value += GERMAN_MULTIPLIERS[word] * 1000
181|            rest = rest[len(word + "tausend"):]

183|    else:

209|    """Resolve a strength label as the reconciler does (SPEC §2, round 2 #1)."""
210|    canonical = canonical_inn(name)
211|    known_moieties = {inn for entry in catalogue.entries for inn in entry.inns}

220|def _grounded_by_turns(field: object, cited: list[str]) -> bool:
221|    """An ingredient field grounded by cited turns (SPEC §2, batch 24)."""
222|    if not isinstance(field, str):
223|        return False
224|    norm_field = normalise(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", field))
225|    if not norm_field:
226|        return False
227|    field_words = norm_field.split()
228|    only_numbers = True
229|    for word in field_words:
230|        if word in UNIT_WORDS or word in _AMOUNT_ONLY_WORDS or stated_amounts(word) or has_number_role(word):
231|            continue
232|        if word.isdigit():
233|            continue
234|        only_numbers = False
235|        break
236|    if only_numbers:
237|        return False
238|    field_pair = (canonical_inn(field), salt_of(field))
239|    for text in cited:
240|        norm_turn = normalise(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text))
241|        if not norm_turn:
242|            continue
243|        parts = []
244|        for word in field_words:
245|            if re.search(r"[\u0600-\u06ff]", word):
246|                parts.append(f"{ARABIC_CLITICS}{re.escape(word)}")
247|            else:
248|                parts.append(re.escape(word))
249|        if re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + r"\s+".join(parts) + r"(?!\w)", norm_turn):
250|            return True
251|        turn_words = norm_turn.split()
252|        matched = True
253|        for word in field_words:
254|            if len(word) < 3:
255|                if word not in turn_words:
256|                    matched = False
257|                    break
258|                continue
259|            stem = word[:-1] if len(word) >= 6 and word[-1] in "aeiou" else word
260|            if not any(turn_word.startswith(stem) for turn_word in turn_words):
261|                matched = False
262|                break
263|        if matched:
264|            return True
265|        for start in range(len(turn_words)):
266|            for size in (1, 2, 3):
267|                run = " ".join(turn_words[start:start + size])
268|                if not run:
269|                    continue
270|                if (canonical_inn(run), salt_of(run)) == field_pair:
271|                    return True
272|    return False

275|def _grounded_label(field: object, cited: list[str], catalogue: Catalogue, name_text: object) -> bool:
276|    """An amount label grounded by turns or by the brand's own ingredients."""
277|    if _grounded_by_turns(field, cited):
278|        return True
279|    if not isinstance(field, str) or not isinstance(name_text, str):
280|        return False
281|    entry = catalogue.resolve(name_text)
282|    return entry is not None and canonical_inn(field) in entry.inns

285|def parse_claims_json(
286|    text: str, turns: list[AudioTurn], catalogue: Catalogue | None = None,
287|) -> list[PatientClaim]:
288|    """Validate Spark JSON and attach only cited transcript turns as evidence."""
289|    cat = catalogue if catalogue is not None else _bundled_catalogue()
290|    try:
291|        raw_claims = _validate_raw_shape(json.loads(text))
292|        transcripts = {turn.turn_id: turn.transcript for turn in turns}
293|        claims = []
294|        for index, raw in enumerate(raw_claims, start=1):
295|            _check_no_advice(_advice_strings(raw))
296|            assert_no_advice_in_ingredients(raw)
297|            turn_ids = raw["turn_ids"]
298|            invalid_turn_ids = any(
299|                not isinstance(turn_id, str) or turn_id not in transcripts for turn_id in turn_ids
300|            ) if isinstance(turn_ids, list) else True
301|            if not isinstance(turn_ids, list) or not turn_ids or invalid_turn_ids:
302|                raise ValueError("claim turn_ids must cite existing turns")
303|            _check_grounded(raw["name_text"], turn_ids, transcripts)
304|            cited = [transcripts[turn_id] for turn_id in turn_ids]
305|            raw_inn = raw.get("inn")
306|            if raw_inn is None:
307|                grounded_inn: Any = None
308|            elif isinstance(raw_inn, str):
309|                grounded_inn = raw_inn if _grounded_by_turns(raw_inn, cited) else None
310|            else:
311|                grounded_inn = raw_inn
312|            raw_intake = raw["intake_amount"]
313|            if isinstance(raw_intake, dict):
314|                label = raw_intake.get("inn")
315|                if not (
316|                    isinstance(label, str) and _grounded_label(label, cited, cat, raw["name_text"])
317|                ):
318|                    fallback = grounded_inn if isinstance(grounded_inn, str) else raw["name_text"]
319|                    raw_intake = {**raw_intake, "inn": fallback}
320|            raw_strength: Any = raw["strength"]
321|            if isinstance(raw_strength, dict) and isinstance(raw_strength.get("ingredients"), list):
322|                relabelled = []
323|                for part in raw_strength["ingredients"]:
324|                    if isinstance(part, dict):
325|                        label = part.get("inn")
326|                        if isinstance(label, str) and _grounded_label(
327|                            label, cited, cat, raw["name_text"],
328|                        ):
329|                            relabelled.append(part)
330|                        else:
331|                            fallback = (
332|                                grounded_inn if isinstance(grounded_inn, str) else raw["name_text"]
333|                            )
334|                            relabelled.append({**part, "inn": fallback})
335|                    else:
336|                        relabelled.append(part)
337|                raw_strength = {**raw_strength, "ingredients": relabelled}
338|            strength_was_empty = (
339|                isinstance(raw["strength"], dict) and raw["strength"].get("ingredients") == []
340|            )
341|            strength = coerce_strength(raw_strength) if raw_strength is not None else None
342|            if isinstance(strength, dict):
343|                resolved = {
344|                    _resolve_strength_inn(part["inn"], cat) for part in strength["ingredients"]
345|                }
346|                if len(resolved) < len(strength["ingredients"]):
347|                    strength = None
348|            intake_amount = _coerce_intake(raw_intake)
349|            regimen = _coerce_regimen(raw["regimen"])
350|            said: set = set()
351|            for cited_id in turn_ids:
352|                said |= stated_amounts(transcripts[cited_id])
353|            if isinstance(strength, dict) and not all(
354|                part["amount"] in said for part in strength["ingredients"]
355|            ):
356|                strength = None
357|            if isinstance(intake_amount, dict) and intake_amount["amount"] not in said:
358|                intake_amount = None
359|            units_sent = (
360|                isinstance(raw.get("regimen"), dict)
361|                and raw["regimen"].get("units_per_intake") is not None
362|            )
363|            units_dropped = units_sent and (
364|                not isinstance(regimen, dict) or regimen.get("units_per_intake") is None
365|            )
366|            if (raw["strength"] is not None and strength is None and not strength_was_empty) or (
367|                raw["intake_amount"] is not None and intake_amount is None
368|            ) or units_dropped:
369|                # A dropped claim amount takes the other one with it (SPEC §2).
370|                strength = None
371|                intake_amount = None
372|            values = {
373|                **{key: value for key, value in raw.items() if key != "turn_ids"},
374|                "inn": grounded_inn,
375|                "regimen": regimen,
376|                "intake_amount": intake_amount,
377|                "strength": strength,
378|                "claim_id": f"c{index}",
379|                "audio_evidence": turn_ids,
380|            }
381|            claims.append(PatientClaim.model_validate(values))
382|        return claims
383|    except (TypeError, ValueError, ValidationError) as exc:
384|        raise ProviderError("spark", f"malformed patient claims: {exc}", retryable=True) from exc

387|class MetaClaimExtractor:
388|    def __init__(
389|        self, client: MetaClient, guard: SpendGuard, model: str = "muse-spark-1.3",
390|    ) -> None:
391|        if "-contributor" in model.strip().casefold():
392|            raise ValueError("contributor models are not permitted")
393|        self.client = client
394|        self.guard = guard
395|        self.model = model
396|
397|    def extract(self, turns: list[AudioTurn]) -> tuple[list[PatientClaim], ProviderTrace | None]:
398|        if not turns:
399|            return [], None
400|
401|        transcript = "\n".join(
402|            f"[{turn.turn_id} {turn.start_ms}–{turn.end_ms} ms, speaker {turn.speaker or 'unknown'}] "
403|            f"{turn.transcript}"
404|            for turn in turns
405|        )
406|        body = {
407|            "model": self.model,
408|            "reasoning_effort": "low",
409|            "max_tokens": 16000,
410|            "messages": [
411|                {"role": "system", "content": _SYSTEM_PROMPT},
412|                {"role": "user", "content": transcript},
413|            ],
414|            "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {
415|                "name": "patient_claims", "strict": True, "schema": CLAIMS_SCHEMA,
416|            }},
417|        }
418|
419|        estimate = spark_call_estimate(body)
420|
421|        def attempt() -> tuple[list[PatientClaim], ProviderTrace]:
422|            self.guard.check(estimate)
423|            payload, latency_ms = self.client.post("/chat/completions", json=body)
424|            try:
425|                usage = payload["usage"]
426|                input_tokens = int(usage["prompt_tokens"])
427|                output_tokens = int(usage["completion_tokens"])
428|                content = payload["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
429|                call_id = payload["id"]
430|                if not isinstance(call_id, str) or not call_id:
431|                    raise ValueError("missing id")
432|                cost = cost_usd(self.model, input_tokens=input_tokens, output_tokens=output_tokens)
433|            except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
434|                raise ProviderError(
435|                    "spark", "malformed Spark response", retryable=True,
436|                    billable_uncertain=True, estimated_reason="malformed Spark response",
437|                ) from exc
438|            trace = ProviderTrace(
439|                call_id=call_id,
440|                model_id=self.model,
441|                latency_ms=latency_ms,
442|                input_tokens=input_tokens,
443|                output_tokens=output_tokens,
444|                cost_usd=cost,
445|            )
446|            self.guard.charge_prechecked(trace)
447|            if payload["choices"][0].get("finish_reason") == "length":
448|                raise ProviderError(
449|                    "spark", "Spark reply stopped at the length limit", retryable=False,
450|                    attempt_trace=trace,
451|                )
452|            try:
453|                claims = parse_claims_json(content, turns)
454|            except ProviderError as exc:
455|                raise ProviderError(
456|                    exc.provider, self.client._safe(str(exc)), retryable=True,
457|                    attempt_trace=trace,
458|                ) from None
459|            return claims, trace
460|
461|        return with_one_retry(attempt, guard=self.guard, model_id=self.model, estimate=estimate)

event.text:
**Verdict:** Build matches SPEC and contract; no fail-open crash, only narrow fuzzy and minor over-skips.

**Findings:**

1. **Medium — fuzzy drops SPEC's short-name blocks.** `SPEC.md:257` requires turn word ≥4 letters; diff `relations.py` `fuzzy_words={... if len(word)>=4}` also requires name word ≥4. A 1–3 letter alias/INN (e.g. `d`) never blocks past/split, dropping where SPEC keeps. Fix: keep `len(token)>=4`, drop name-word length filter.
2. **Low — walk skips non-units.** `SPEC.md:252` walks over “unit words”; `SPEC.md:239` lists `ملي/مللي/ميكرو` separately. Diff `_UNIT_SKIP=...|_OPEN_UNIT` plus pair fragments (`لتر`,`دوليه`) skips them, so `Panadol ملي five` walks to Panadol and drops; SPEC stops at `ملي` and keeps. Fix: walk only `_UNIT_SINGLE`/`_UNIT_TWO` units.
3. **Low — glued names have no SPEC basis.** `SPEC.md:255` matches whole tokens; diff `_names_to_token_lists` adds `norm.replace(" ","")`. `PanadolExtra` then drops for Panadol where SPEC keeps. Fix: remove glued variant.
4. **Low — `ten mg, a day` kept as non-daily.** `SPEC.md:257` says directly followed; diff `_is_daily_total` requires same clause, so comma breaks daily and split total is kept. Fix: allow one clause break or pin SPEC.
5. **Info — 4-letter reach is huge.** `SPEC.md:257` + diff fuzzy `token.startswith(word) or word.startswith(token)` over every catalogue brand/alias/INN means e.g. Spanish `para` matches `paracetamol` and blocks any splitter/past in its clause, only ever keeping. Per SPEC, but document it.

**What you checked and found fine:**
- Word lists match SPEC: negation/DON (`SPEC.md:242`), mg/mcg/g/ml/iu + open (`SPEC.md:243-250`), counts + `sobre` + ES/DE dose (`SPEC.md:251`), joiners/of (`SPEC.md:252`), past (`SPEC.md:256`), per-day (`SPEC.md:257`), clause ends (`SPEC.md:240`).
- SPEC-keeps cases keep: bare number, open `ملي`, negation ≥3 away, `before breakfast`, `once/twice a day` (not directly followed).
- `claims.py` diff sits between value check and drop-other rule (`anamnesis/providers/claims.py:350-371`), so dropped relation nulls the other; `discontinued` only skips past.
- No change to `stated_amounts`, labels, `regimen`, reconciler; `TypeError/ValueError` still become malformed, no new crash type.
